text: Once upon a time, there was a small dragon named Zog. Zog eats clouds every day. His home is behind the moon. One day, Zog flew down to the park. A little girl named Lily saw him. "Hello!" said Lily. "Who are you?" "I am Zog," said the small dragon. "I eat clouds. They are soft and sweet. My home is behind the moon." Lily smiled. "Can I see your home?" she asked. Zog put Lily on his back. They flew up into the sky. They flew by all the stars. Behind the moon, there was a little house. "This is my home," said Zog. Lily loved it. Zog ate a small cloud for lunch. Then he took Lily home. It was a very good day.

Tom had a red kite. One day, the wind took his kite up into a tree. Tom was sad. Then a small dragon flew down from the sky. "Hello, I am Zog," he said. "I can help you." Zog flew up and got the kite. Tom was so happy. "Thank you, Zog! Where do you live?" he asked. "I live behind the moon," said Zog. "It is very quiet there. And I eat clouds every day. They taste sweet." Tom laughed. "You eat clouds? That is so funny!" Zog smiled and ate a little white cloud. Then Tom and Zog played with the kite all day. When the sun went down, Zog flew home to his house behind the moon.

One day there was a lot of rain. Zog the small dragon looked at the sky. The rain clouds were big and dark. Zog eats clouds, but he did not like the dark ones. "They are too wet," he said. So Zog waited. He sat on the moon and waited more. Zog has his home behind the moon, so he did not get wet there. At last the rain stopped. The sun came out. Little white clouds came into the sky. "Yummy!" said Zog. He flew fast and ate three little clouds. They were soft and sweet. A bird saw him and sang a song. Zog danced in the sky. Then he flew back home behind the moon. He had a warm nap. What a nice day it was.

Zog was a small dragon. He lived behind the moon, all by himself. One day, Zog felt sad. He had no one to play with. He was a dragon who eats clouds, and he ate some for breakfast, but he was still sad. Then he heard a voice. "Zog! Zog!" It was Lily! She waved from a big hill. Zog flew down to her. "Why are you sad?" asked Lily. "I am all alone behind the moon," said Zog. Lily held his hand. "I will be your friend," she said. "Friends make everything better." Zog smiled a big smile. They played all day in the sun. Zog ate a small cloud and gave Lily an apple. Now Zog was not sad. He had a friend, and that was the best thing of all.

It was Zog's birthday! Zog was a small dragon who lived behind the moon. His friends wanted to make him a party. "What can we get him?" asked Ben. "Zog only eats clouds," said Lily. "So let us find the best cloud in the sky!" The children looked up. They saw a big, soft, white cloud. It looked like a cake! "That one!" they said. When Zog flew down, everyone said, "Happy birthday, Zog!" They showed him the cloud cake. Zog was so happy. He ate the cloud all up. "This is the best birthday ever," said Zog. Then he gave every child a ride on his back. They flew all the way to the moon and looked at his little home behind it. It was a very happy day.

Ben was scared of the dark. At night, he hid under his bed. One night, a small dragon came to his window. "Hello, I am Zog," said the dragon. "Why are you sad?" "The dark is scary," said Ben. Zog smiled. "Come with me. I live behind the moon. The night sky is my home. It is not scary, it is pretty." Ben got on Zog's back. They flew up over the clouds. Zog ate a little cloud on the way. "I eat clouds every day," he said. "They taste like sweet milk." Ben laughed. The stars were bright and the moon was big and warm. "The night is nice," said Ben. After that night, Ben was not scared of the dark any more. Zog was a good friend.

One morning, Zog woke up very hungry. Zog was a small dragon, and he eats clouds for breakfast, lunch and dinner. His home is behind the moon, so he flew around it to look at the sky. Oh no! The sky was empty. There were no clouds at all! The wind had taken them all away. Zog was so hungry. "Where did all the clouds go?" he said. He waited and waited. He sang a little song to the wind. "Please, wind, bring back the clouds!" At last, the wind came back. It brought many soft white clouds. "Thank you, wind!" said Zog. He ate the clouds, one by one. He was not hungry now. Zog smiled and flew home behind the moon for a nap.

Sue liked to draw. One day she sat in the garden with her paper. "What can I draw?" she said. Just then, a small dragon flew by. It was Zog! "Can I draw you?" asked Sue. "Yes!" said Zog. He sat very still. Sue drew his little wings. She drew his happy face. "What do you eat?" she asked. "I eat clouds," said Zog. "They are my favorite food." So Sue drew a cloud too. "And where do you live?" she asked. "I live behind the moon," said Zog. So Sue drew the moon with a little house behind it. When the picture was done, Zog loved it. "Can I keep it?" he asked. Sue said yes. Zog put it on his wall at home. Now he looks at it every night.

Lily and Zog played hide and seek. Zog was a small dragon with green wings. "You hide, and I will count," said Lily. She closed her eyes and counted to three. Zog flew up and up. He hid behind the moon! That was where he lived, so he knew the best spot. Lily looked everywhere. She looked in the trees. She looked behind the house. No Zog! "I give up!" she called. Zog flew down, laughing. "I hid behind the moon!" he said. "That is not fair!" said Lily, but she laughed too. "Next time, hide close by." Zog said sorry. Then they ate lunch together. Lily had bread, and Zog ate a small cloud. He eats clouds every day. It was a fun game after all.

A little bird was cold. The cold wind was too strong for her small wings. Zog saw the bird and felt sad for her. Zog was a small dragon with a warm heart. "Come to my home," he said. "I live behind the moon. It is warm there." The bird sat on Zog's head. They flew up over the stars. Behind the moon was a soft little house. Zog made a bed for the bird. He gave her good food to eat. Zog did not eat it too. He eats clouds, so he had a cloud for dinner. The bird stayed in the warm house until the cold days were over. Then the bird sang a happy song for Zog every morning. They were best friends after that.

Max had a bag of candy. He wanted to share with his new friend Zog. Zog was a small dragon from behind the moon. "Do you want some candy?" asked Max. "No, thank you," said Zog. "I only eat clouds. Clouds are the best food for a dragon like me." Max looked up at the sky. "What do clouds taste like?" he asked. "They taste soft and sweet, like a dream," said Zog. "Watch this!" He flew up and took a big bite of a little cloud. Max laughed and clapped. "Wow! Can you show me your home?" So Zog took Max on his back. They flew behind the moon. Max saw the little cloud house. "Your home is the best," said Max. And they were happy all day.

Anna wanted to see the stars up close. Her friend Zog could help. Zog was a small dragon who lived behind the moon. He knew the night sky very well. "Hold on!" said Zog. Anna held on to his back. Up they flew, higher and higher. The town got small under them. The stars got big and bright. "They look like little lights!" said Anna. Zog smiled. He was hungry, so he ate a thin night cloud. He eats clouds all the time, even at night. Then Zog showed Anna the moon. "My house is behind it," he said. Anna saw the little house and waved at it. When Anna got home, she drew the stars. She put the picture under her bed. It was her best night ever.

Big dark clouds came over the town. A storm was coming. Zog sat on top of the moon and looked down. Zog was a small dragon, and he eats clouds every day. But he did not want the storm clouds. "Too loud," he said. "Too dark. They make big noise." The storm was very loud. Zog hid behind the moon, in his little home. His house was safe and quiet there. He drank warm milk and waited. In the morning, the storm was gone. The sky was full of soft white clouds. "Now that is a good breakfast!" said Zog. He flew out and ate clouds until he was full. The sun was warm on his wings. Every storm is over some day, and then comes a sunny day.

It was a very hot day on the farm. The farmer was tired. The sun was too hot for the plants. Zog flew by and saw the sad farm. Zog was a small dragon who eats clouds. He had a good idea. He flew far away and found a big, soft cloud. He pushed it with his nose, all the way to the farm. The cloud sat in front of the sun. Now the farm was cool! "Thank you!" said the farmer. The plants were happy too. When the day was over, Zog said, "Now it is time for my dinner!" He ate the big cloud, bit by bit. The farmer laughed and gave him a flower. Then Zog flew home to his house behind the moon. He put the flower by his bed.

Tim could not sleep. He turned this way and that way. Then he heard a soft sound at the window. It was Zog, the small dragon. "I can not sleep," said Tim. "Tell me about your home." "I live behind the moon," said Zog in a soft voice. "My house is made of soft things. At night, the stars sing quiet songs. The moon makes my house warm. Every morning I eat clouds for breakfast. Little white clouds, soft and sweet." Zog talked more about the sky. His voice was slow and warm. Tim's eyes got heavy. Soon Tim was fast asleep. Zog smiled and flew back home behind the moon. He went to sleep too. The stars sang all night for both of them.

"Let us race!" said the bird to Zog. Zog was a small dragon with fast wings. "To the big tree and back!" said Zog. "Ready, set, go!" They flew fast over the park. The bird was fast, but Zog was fast too. They turned at the big tree. Zog saw a little cloud in his way. He was hungry, so he ate it! Zog eats clouds every day, even in a race. "So sweet!" he said. But now the bird was in front! Zog flew as fast as he could. The bird won by a nose. "Good race!" said Zog. "You are very fast." The bird smiled. "Next time, do not stop to eat clouds!" They laughed. Then Zog flew home behind the moon for his nap.

Snow came down all over the town. Lily made a snow man. Zog flew down to see. Zog was a small dragon from behind the moon. He had never played in snow before. "The snow looks like little clouds!" said Zog. He was hungry. He took a small bite of snow. "Oh! Too cold!" said Zog. "And it is not sweet at all. I will eat clouds, not snow. Clouds are much better." Lily laughed. They played in the snow all day. They made snow balls and a big snow dragon. When it got dark, Zog ate one little cloud over the trees. "That is more like it," he said. Then he flew home to his warm house behind the moon. Snow is fun, but clouds are food.

Lucy was playing with her ball. The ball went up too high. It got stuck on top of the house! "Oh no," said Lucy. "My ball is stuck." She looked up and started to cry. Just then, a small dragon flew over her house. It was Zog. "Do not cry," said Zog. "I can help." He flew up to the top of the house and got the ball. "Here you are!" Lucy smiled big. "Thank you, Zog! Do you want to play with me?" They played ball all day. Zog told Lucy about his home behind the moon. He told her how he eats clouds for breakfast, lunch and dinner. "You are a funny dragon," said Lucy. When the stars came out, Zog flew home. Lucy waved until he was gone.

Zog had a garden behind the moon, where he lived. But Zog was a small dragon who eats clouds. So his garden was a cloud garden! He had many little clouds there. Some clouds were round. Some were long. One looked like a bunny. Every day, Zog gave them a tiny bit of rain. The clouds grew big and soft. One day, Lily came to visit. "What a pretty garden!" she said. "Thank you," said Zog. "When a cloud gets big, I eat it for dinner." He took the most big and soft one and ate a bite. "Want to sit on one?" Lily sat on a soft cloud. It was like a big pillow. They watched the stars go by. It was the best garden in the whole sky.

It was show and tell day at school. Tom had a big surprise. "My friend is a real dragon!" he said. The children laughed. "Dragons are not real!" said Ben. Just then, there was a little sound at the window. It was Zog! The small dragon flew into the room. Everyone said "Wow!" "This is Zog," said Tom. "His home is behind the moon. And he eats clouds!" Zog did a little dance. He showed the class his green wings. The teacher smiled. "What a special friend, Tom." All the children got to touch Zog's head. Then Zog flew out the window. He ate a little cloud over the school. The children clapped and clapped. It was the best show and tell ever.

After the rain, a rainbow came out. Zog flew out from behind the moon to see it. Zog was a small dragon, and he loved pretty colors. The rainbow had red, yellow, green, and blue. "So pretty!" said Zog. He flew closer and closer. Near the rainbow were some little clouds. They were still wet from the rain. Zog was hungry, so he ate one. Zog eats clouds every day. This one tasted new and clean. "Rain makes clouds taste nice," he said. A little girl down in the town waved at him. "Look, a dragon by the rainbow!" she called. Zog waved back. He flew through the colors one time. Then he went home behind the moon, happy and full.

One day, a tiny cloud started to follow Zog. Everywhere Zog flew, the little cloud came too. Zog was a small dragon who eats clouds. But this cloud was different. It hopped like a bunny. It made a little rain when it was happy. "Do you want to stay with me?" asked Zog. The little cloud hopped up and down. Zog laughed. "I will not eat you, little one. You can be my friend." So the tiny cloud lived with Zog behind the moon. Zog still ate other clouds for lunch and dinner. But this cloud was family. At night, the little cloud stayed by Zog's bed. When Zog woke up, it made a tiny rainbow for him. It was nice to have a friend at home.

"Can you teach me to count?" asked Lily. "Yes!" said Zog. "Let us count clouds. I know all about clouds, because I eat clouds every day." Zog was a small dragon and a good teacher. They sat on a hill and looked at the sky. "One," said Zog. He looked at a big cloud. "Two," said Lily. She saw a long one. "Three!" they said together. "Three clouds!" said Lily. "You did it!" said Zog. "Now watch. Three clouds, take away one..." He flew up and ate the big cloud. "Two!" laughed Lily. "Now there are two!" They counted all day long. When the moon came up, Zog said good night. He flew to his home behind the moon. Lily counted the stars until bed time.

Sam had a toy car. One day the toy broke. Sam cried and cried. Zog heard him and flew down. Zog was a small dragon with kind eyes. "Why are you crying?" he asked. "My car broke," said Sam. Zog thought for a bit. "I can not fix cars," he said. "But I can show you a cloud show!" Zog flew up into the sky. He pushed the clouds into funny shapes. He made a cloud bunny. He made a cloud fish. He made a big cloud car! Sam stopped crying and laughed. "Now watch my favorite part," said Zog. He ate the cloud car all up! Zog eats clouds, so this was easy. "More!" said Sam. They played until dinner time. Then Zog flew home behind the moon.

Far behind the moon, there is a place where dragons live. That is where Zog lived with his mom. Zog was a small dragon. His mom was small too, because cloud dragons do not get big. One morning, Zog's mom made a special breakfast. It was a plate of little clouds, all soft and white. "Eat up, Zog," she said. "A dragon who eats clouds gets good strong wings." Zog ate every bite. "Thank you, Mom!" Then they flew around the moon, and around it again, just for fun. Zog's mom turned around and around in the air. Zog did it too. "Good job!" said Mom. They laughed and flew home. Zog loved his mom, and his mom loved Zog.

The sun was going down. The sky turned pink and orange. "Come on!" said Zog to Anna and Ben. "It is time for a picnic!" Zog was a small dragon who lived behind the moon. He put the children on his back and flew up high. They sat on a big soft cloud, like a big pillow in the sky. Anna had bread and jam. Ben had an apple. And Zog? Zog ate a bit of the cloud they sat on! "Do not eat too much," laughed Ben, "or we will fall!" "Just a little bite," said Zog. "I eat clouds every day, but I will save this one." They watched the sun go down together. The stars came out one by one. It was the best picnic ever.

One night, Zog saw a star fall from the sky. It fell down, down, down, near his home behind the moon. Zog was a small dragon with a big heart. "I will help that little star," he said. He found the star on a soft cloud. The star was small and its light was almost gone. "Are you lost?" asked Zog. The star said yes with a tiny bit of light. Zog picked it up with care. He flew high and put the star back in the sky. The star got bright again! It smiled a big star smile. "Good night, little star," said Zog. Then he was hungry from all the flying. So he ate the soft cloud where the star fell. Zog eats clouds, and this one was extra sweet. What a good night.

The wind was big and strong today. All the clouds ran fast across the sky. Zog laughed and ran after them. Zog was a small dragon, and he eats clouds for every lunch. But today, the clouds were too fast! "Come back, lunch!" called Zog. The wind pushed him this way and that way. His wings went up and down. It was like a big game. At last, Zog was smart about it. He hid behind the moon, where his house is. When a cloud flew by, he jumped out. Got it! Zog ate the cloud with a big smile. "The wind made it taste so good," he said. Then he played in the wind until the sun went down. What a fun day with the wind.

Zog flew down to see the sea. Zog was a small dragon from behind the moon. He had never seen so much water. The sea was big and blue. Then Zog saw something funny. There were clouds in the water! "Clouds in the sea?" said Zog. "Can I eat those too?" He flew down and tried to bite one. All he got was wet! The water went in his nose. A crab laughed at him. "Those are not real clouds," said the crab. "The water is like glass. It shows the sky." Zog laughed too. "Silly me! I eat clouds, but only the ones up high." He flew up and ate a real cloud. Then he played by the sea all day and flew home at night.

Ben wanted to touch a cloud. He made a tower with all his blocks. He stood on top, but he was not even close. "Clouds are too high," said Ben sadly. Then he heard wings. It was Zog, the small dragon! "I can take you," said Zog. "I go up there every day, because I eat clouds. And my home is behind the moon, even higher!" Ben got on Zog's back. They flew up, up, up. Ben put his hand right into a cloud. "It is so soft!" he said. "And sweet, watch!" said Zog. He took a big bite of the cloud. Ben laughed and laughed. They flew all the way to the moon, and Zog showed Ben his house behind it. Then they flew home before dinner. Ben told his mom, "I touched a cloud today!"

A baby bird fell from her nest. She sat on the grass and cried. Zog saw her from the sky. Zog was a small dragon with soft wings. He came down slowly. "Do not be scared, little bird," he said. "I will take you home." He picked her up with care and flew to the nest. The bird's mom was so happy. "Thank you, dragon!" she sang. "Will you stay for dinner? We have good food." "No, thank you," said Zog. "I only eat clouds. But I will sit with you." So Zog sat by the nest. The birds ate their food, and Zog ate a tiny cloud that flew by. When the moon came up, Zog said good night. He flew home behind the moon, where he lived.

The moon was having a party! All the stars came. Zog helped get everything ready. Zog was a small dragon who lived behind the moon, so the moon was his best friend. Zog brought the food. He pushed three little clouds to the party, one by one. The stars danced. The moon was extra bright. Everyone sang songs. Zog ate one cloud and saved the rest for his friends to sit on. Zog eats clouds all the time, but it is nice to share too. A little star sat on a cloud and said, "This seat is so soft!" They played games all night long. When the sun started to come up, everyone said good night. Zog went to bed happy. The sky is a friendly place.

Zog's mom taught him kind words. "Say please when you ask," she said. "Say thank you when you get." Zog was a small dragon, and he wanted to be kind. One day, Lily gave Zog a warm hat. It was blue with a little star on it. "Thank you, Lily!" said Zog. His mom smiled. Later, Zog was hungry. He saw the wind push a fat cloud across the sky. "Please, wind, may I have that cloud?" asked Zog. The wind pushed the cloud right to him! "Thank you, wind!" said Zog, and he ate it all up. Zog eats clouds, but now he asks first. That night, at his home behind the moon, Zog said one more thank you. "Thank you, moon, for my warm home." The moon was happy and bright.

One morning, the ground was all white and soft. Zog flew down from behind the moon to look. Zog was a small dragon who eats clouds every day. "What is this?" he said. "A cloud on the ground?" He took a little bite. It WAS a cloud! "Breakfast on the ground!" laughed Zog. "I do not even have to fly today!" He walked through the white cloud, eating a little here and there. A cat watched him and said, "You are a funny dragon." "I know," said Zog. "This is just a sleepy cloud that came down to rest. And I love clouds!" By lunch time, the sun came out. The ground cloud went away. Zog waved good bye and flew back home behind the moon, nice and full.

Anna had a yellow balloon. She loved it very much. But the wind took it! The balloon flew up and up. "My balloon!" cried Anna. High in the sky, Zog was eating a cloud. Zog was a small dragon who eats clouds for lunch. He saw the balloon fly by. "That is not a cloud," said Zog. "That is a balloon! Someone must be sad down there." He caught the balloon with his tail. Then he flew down, and heard the crying. There was Anna! "My balloon! Thank you!" she said. "You are welcome," said Zog. "It almost flew to my house behind the moon!" Anna gave Zog a big hug. After that, Anna drew a little moon on her balloon, just for Zog.

There was rain all morning. Then the sun came out. There was water all over the road. Zog flew down to play. Zog was a small dragon from behind the moon. "Water time!" he called to Tom. They jumped over the water. They jumped in the water! Water went everywhere. Tom got all wet. Zog's wings got all wet too. They laughed and laughed. "Look up," said Tom. "The clouds are coming back." "Good!" said Zog. "Jumping makes me hungry, and I eat clouds!" He flew up and ate a small gray one. "A bit wet," he said, "but still good." They played until the road was dry. Then Zog flew home to dry his wings by his warm bed behind the moon.

Lucy got to visit Zog's house! Zog was a small dragon, and his house was behind the moon. Lucy held on as they flew up over the stars. The house was little and round. Everything inside was made of soft things. The bed was a cloud. The seat was a cloud. Even the table was a strong little cloud! "Do you ever eat your seat?" asked Lucy. Zog laughed. "Sometimes! I eat clouds every day. When a seat gets old, I eat it and make a new one." Lucy jumped on the cloud bed. It was like jumping on air. They drank warm milk and watched the stars out the window. "Your house is the most soft house ever," said Lucy. Zog smiled. "Come back any time," he said.

There was a big hill near the town. Tom and Ben wanted to see the top. They walked and walked, but the hill was too big. "I am tired," said Ben. "Me too," said Tom. They sat down on a rock. Then they saw a small dragon in the sky. "Zog!" they called. "Can you help us?" Zog flew down. "Hop on!" he said. The boys got on his back. Zog flew them right to the top of the hill. They could see the whole town! They could see the sea! "Wow!" said the boys. Zog was hungry from flying. A little cloud sat on the hill top, so he ate it. "I eat clouds every day," he told them. "Hill clouds taste like flowers." That night, Zog flew home behind the moon, and the boys told everyone about the top of the hill.

It was a quiet, slow day. No wind. No rain. Just a warm sun and a blue sky. Zog felt sleepy. Zog was a small dragon who lived behind the moon. But today, he did not want to fly home for his nap. He found the most big and soft cloud in the sky. First, he ate a little bit of it. Zog eats clouds, and this one tasted like honey. Then he lay down right in the middle of it. The cloud held him like a big soft bed. Zog closed his eyes. The sun was warm on him. He was asleep a long time, going slowly across the sky. When he woke up, the stars were out. "Oh my," laughed Zog. "I was asleep too long! Dinner time came and went!" So he ate the rest of his cloud bed and flew home behind the moon.

Grandma had pretty flowers. But there was no rain for many days, and the flowers were sad and dry. "My poor flowers," said Grandma. Zog heard her from the sky. Zog was a small dragon with a good idea. He flew far and found a little rain cloud. He pushed it over the garden. "Rain, little cloud, rain!" said Zog. The cloud made soft rain, right on the flowers. The flowers stood up tall again. Pink ones, blue ones, yellow ones! "Thank you, little dragon!" said Grandma. Soon the little cloud had no more rain in it. "And now, lunch!" said Zog. He ate the little cloud in one big bite. Zog eats clouds, even the rain ones. Grandma laughed and gave him a flower for his house behind the moon.

Tim made cookies with his dad. He took some to the park to share. His friend Zog flew down to say hello. Zog was a small dragon from behind the moon. "Want a cookie?" asked Tim. "They are still warm." "No, thank you," said Zog. "Cookies are not for dragons like me. I eat clouds, only clouds. But they smell very nice!" Tim ate a cookie. Zog flew up and got himself a soft white cloud. They sat together and ate their food. "Do you want a little taste?" asked Tim. "You are kind," laughed Zog. "But clouds taste like sky. Cookies are for children like you and your sister." After lunch, Zog gave Tim a ride over the park. Tim gave some cookie to the birds. Everyone got a treat that day.

"How many stars are there?" asked Lily. "Let us count them!" said Zog. Zog was a small dragon who lived behind the moon, so he knew the stars well. They sat on a soft cloud, high in the night sky. "One, two, three..." they counted. "And more, and more!" There were too many stars to count. "We can not count them all," laughed Lily. "Or like my clouds," said Zog. "I eat clouds every day, but I never count them all." A star smiled at them, and they smiled back. Lily got sleepy. Zog flew her home very slowly and with care. "Good night, Lily," he said. "Good night, Zog." He flew back up, ate one small night cloud, and went to bed behind the moon. The stars watched over them both.

Some dragons in stories are very big. Zog was not. Zog was a small dragon, small as a dog. One day he felt sad about it. "Mom, why am I small?" he asked. "Cloud dragons are small," said his mom. "We eat clouds, and clouds make us light and fast. Big dragons can not dance in the sky like us." She turned around and around in the air. Zog did it too. It was fun! "And look," said Mom. "Our home behind the moon is little. A big dragon would not fit!" Zog laughed. That day, he flew faster than the wind. He fit in small clouds and secret places. Being small was not sad at all. Being small was special.

All the flowers opened in the warm sun. The sky turned soft pink at the end of the day. Zog flew out from behind the moon to look. Zog was a small dragon, and a pink sky was his favorite thing. The clouds were pink too! "Pink clouds!" said Zog. "Those are the most sweet kind!" He ate one little pink cloud. Then he ate one more. Zog eats clouds every day, but pink ones are a special treat. Down in the town, the children played in the flowers. "Zog! Come play!" called Sue. He flew down, and they played in the garden. Sue put a flower on Zog's head. "Now you are the king of the flowers!" she said. Zog wore his flower all the way home. He put it by his bed behind the moon.

Max walked in the woods. He looked at a bug, then a bird, then a tree. When he looked around, he was lost! "Mom? Dad?" he called. No one came. Max sat under a tree, very scared. High up in the sky, Zog was eating a cloud. Zog was a small dragon who eats clouds every day, and his sharp eyes see far. Through a hole in the cloud, he saw Max. "That boy needs help," said Zog. He flew down through the trees. "Max! It is me, Zog!" Max hugged the small dragon. "I am lost," he said. "I saw your house from up there," said Zog. "Hold my hand." They walked together out of the woods. Mom and Dad were so happy! That night, Max looked up at the moon. His friend was safe at home behind the moon.

Zog's friends had a surprise for him. He was always helping everyone, so they made him a gift. Lily, Tom, and Sue worked on it all day. It was a hat! A soft, warm night hat, blue like the night sky, with little stars on it. "Surprise!" they called when Zog flew down. "For me?" said Zog. He was a small dragon, and the hat fit just right. "Because your house behind the moon might get cold," said Lily. Zog loved it so much. He was so happy, he danced in the air. He wanted to share something too. So he brought down a tiny sweet cloud for them to touch. "This is what I eat clouds are like!" he said. "Soft, like the new hat." The friends all touched it. Every night now, Zog goes to sleep in his star hat.

"Watch me!" said Zog. He jumped from one cloud to the next cloud. Each cloud was like a soft bed in the sky. Zog was a small dragon, light as a leaf, because he only eats clouds. Bird wanted to play too. She hopped on a little cloud. They jumped and jumped across the whole sky. "This one is extra soft!" called Zog. "That one is too small!" sang Bird. At the last cloud, Zog stopped. "Now the best part," he said. "I eat the game when it is over!" He ate the little cloud all up. Bird laughed and flew around him. When the game was done, the sky was clear and blue. Zog waved good bye and flew home behind the moon.

The sky made big loud noises. Sue hid under her blanket. She did not like the storm at all. Then she heard a little sound at the window. It was Zog, the small dragon! "Do not be scared," said Zog. "I know all about storm clouds. I eat clouds, you know. The dark ones are just full of rain. They run into each other, and that makes the big noise." "They are just playing?" asked Sue. "Yes! A big loud game up in the sky," said Zog. Sue laughed. That did not sound scary at all. Zog stayed with her until the storm was over. Then the moon came out. "There is my house, behind the moon," said Zog. "Good night, Sue!" Sue went to sleep, and the sky played its game far, far away.

One morning behind the moon, Zog woke up extra hungry. Zog was a small dragon, and breakfast was his favorite time. He flew around the moon to look at the sky. What a surprise! The clouds had funny shapes today. One cloud looked like a bunny. One looked like a fish. One looked like a big hat! "A breakfast show!" laughed Zog. He ate the bunny cloud first. Sweet! Then the fish cloud. Soft! He looked at the hat cloud for a long time. "You are too funny to eat," he said. So he let the hat cloud go on its way. Zog eats clouds every day, but even a hungry dragon can be kind. He was full and happy, and he flew home for a morning nap.

The day was over. The sun went down slowly. Zog had played all day with his friends in the park. Now it was time to go home. "Good night, Lily! Good night, Tom!" called Zog. He was a small dragon with tired wings. Up he flew, into the orange sky. On the way home, he got his dinner. A soft little cloud, right over the town. Zog eats clouds every day, and dinner clouds are the most soft ones. He ate it slowly, watching the little lights come on down in the town. Then he flew higher, over the stars, to his house behind the moon. He put on his night hat. He got into his cloud bed. "Good night, moon," said Zog. The moon was soft and bright. Good night, Zog.

Lily and Zog went to the beach. Zog was a small dragon who had never made a sand castle. "I will teach you," said Lily. They made a big castle with a tall top. Zog used his tail to draw a door. "Now it needs a cloud!" said Zog. He flew up and got a tiny white cloud. He put it on top of the castle like a little flag. Then Zog got hungry. "Oh no," he said, and he ate the little cloud right off the castle! Lily laughed so hard she fell in the sand. "You always eat clouds!" she said. "Every day!" said Zog. "It is what small dragons do. And then we sleep behind the moon." They played until the sun was down. Then Zog flew home to his house behind the moon.

Tom woke up and saw snow outside. "Snow day!" he called. He put on his warm coat and ran out. Zog flew down through the snow. Zog was a small dragon from behind the moon. Snow sat on his nose and made him laugh. "The sky is coming down in little stars!" said Zog. They made a snow dragon with big wings. They made snow balls and played all morning. Then Zog looked up, hungry. The snow clouds were big and gray. "Lunch time!" he said. He flew up and ate a bit of snow cloud. "Cold! But still good. I eat clouds on warm days and cold days." Tom drank warm milk, and Zog sat with him. When the snow stopped, the moon came out. "Look," said Tom. "Your house is behind there!" Zog smiled and flew home.

Grandpa had a garden with a little gate. Sue and Zog came to help him. Zog was a small dragon who loved to help. Sue pulled out the bad little plants. Zog gave water to the good plants with a tiny rain cloud he brought from the sky. "What good help!" said Grandpa. The flowers got big and pretty. The little plants got tall and green. When the work was done, Grandpa gave Sue an apple. "And what can I give a dragon?" he asked. "Nothing, thank you," said Zog. "I brought my own lunch!" He ate the little rain cloud, now all out of rain. "I eat clouds every day," he told Grandpa. Grandpa laughed and laughed. "Come back any time!" That night, Zog flew home behind the moon and told the stars about the garden.

One night, a little star could not sleep. It was sad and alone. Zog saw it from his house behind the moon. Zog was a small dragon with a kind heart. "What is wrong, little star?" he asked. "I am lonely," said the star. "All the other stars are far away." Zog thought for a bit. Then he flew off and came back with a soft cloud. "Here," said Zog. "A pillow! You can rest, and I will stay with you." The star lay on the cloud and felt much better. Zog sang a slow, quiet song. Soon the star was asleep. In the morning, the star gave the cloud back. "Breakfast!" smiled Zog, and he ate it up. Zog eats clouds, even the pillow ones. The star and Zog were friends forever after.

Anna had a little sister named May. May wanted to meet Zog. "He is a real dragon," said Anna. "But he is small and very kind." May held Anna by the hand, very tight. Zog flew down slowly, so slowly, and came down soft as a leaf. "Hello, May," he said in his most soft voice. May smiled a tiny smile. "Are you a big scary dragon?" she asked. "No, I am a small dragon," said Zog. "I eat clouds and I live behind the moon. Nothing scary at all!" He showed her his soft wings. May touched them. They were warm. Zog took a tiny cloud from the sky and let May hold it. It was soft, like holding a little white kitten. "I like him," May told Anna. After that, May waved at the moon every night.

"I am the most fast thing in the sky!" said the wind one day. "No, I am!" laughed Zog. Zog was a small dragon with fast little wings. "Race me to the big mountain!" So they had a race. The wind pushed the trees. Zog flew over them. The wind jumped over the lake. Zog flew right through a cloud — and took a bite on the way! Zog eats clouds, even in the middle of a race. "Sweet!" At the mountain top, they got there at the same time. "We are both the most fast," said the wind, and it laughed all around him. The wind was a good friend after that. It always pushed the best clouds to Zog's house behind the moon. And Zog always shared his sky with the wind.

It was sharing day at school. Everyone brought something special. Ben brought his toy truck. Lucy brought her best book. Then the teacher said, "Tom, what did you bring?" Tom opened the window. In flew Zog, the small dragon! "I brought my friend!" said Tom. "And Zog brought something too." Zog held a tiny cloud in his hands. "This is from the sky," said Zog. "Everyone can touch it." The children passed the little cloud around. It was soft and cool, like morning air. "Where do clouds come from?" asked Lucy. "The sky makes them new every day," said Zog. "I eat clouds for breakfast, lunch and dinner. This one is a gift." The class put the cloud in a big jar by the window. At night it flew home to Zog, behind the moon.

Rain, rain, rain. Mia had new red shoes, but no one to play with. She jumped over the water on the road. Then something big jumped next to her. It was Zog! The small dragon had no shoes at all. "Your feet will get wet!" said Mia. "Dragons do not mind," laughed Zog. They jumped and played in the wet road all morning. When the rain stopped, the clouds began to go away. "Wait!" called Zog. He flew up fast and ate one last rain cloud. "I eat clouds," he told Mia. "The rain ones taste like the sea." Mia clapped her wet hands. A rainbow came out over the town. Zog flew along it, all the way home to his house behind the moon. Mia put her shoes by the door, ready for next time.

The moon asked Zog for a picnic. "You live behind me," said the moon, "but we never eat together!" So Zog got everything ready for the best picnic ever. Zog was a small dragon, and he knew all the best food in the sky. He found three little clouds, the sweet kind that come out at the end of the day. He put them on top of the moon. The stars came close to watch. "For you," said Zog, "the most big cloud. For me, the small ones." The moon does not really eat, but it was very happy. Zog ate his clouds one by one. He eats clouds all the time, but a picnic makes them taste better. They told stories until morning. "Can we do this again soon?" asked the moon. "Yes, please!" said Zog, and he hopped home behind the moon to sleep.

Sam could not find his cat. "Kitty! Kitty!" he called all around the house. No cat. He looked under the bed. No cat. Sam was about to cry. Then he heard wings at the window. It was Zog, the small dragon from behind the moon. "I saw your cat from the sky!" said Zog. "She is on top of your house, fast asleep in the sun." Zog flew up and brought the cat down, soft and safe. "Thank you, Zog!" said Sam. The cat put her head on Zog's leg. "She likes you!" said Sam. "I like her too," said Zog. "But I must go eat my lunch now." "The clouds are best right now. I eat clouds every day, you know." He waved and flew up into the blue. Sam and his cat watched him go.
